atAGlance: Hủ tiếu khô is dry hủ tiếu noodles, usually with minced pork, shrimp or slices, herbs, sauce, and broth on the side.
whatItIs: Hủ tiếu khô is the dry version of southern hủ tiếu: noodles tossed with savory seasoning, toppings, herbs, and often a separate clear broth on the side.
howToEnjoy: Mix the noodles first so the dressing coats them, then sip the side broth between bites. Add lime, chili, and greens slowly so the dry bowl keeps its balance.
howLocalsOrder: Order hủ tiếu khô when you want the noodle flavor concentrated instead of in soup. Ask for soup on the side if it is not obvious, and say less chili before mixing.
worthKnowing: Khô means dry, but the order often still includes broth separately; that two-part rhythm is the point.
goodToKnow: Khô means dry-style, but the broth still matters. Many southern shops serve it on the side so you get both chewy dressed noodles and a clean pork-seafood broth.
